cards.text: This prayer comes with a label on top: it's for one who is afflicted, when he grows faint and pours out his lament before the LORD. No name, no title, just a worn-out man talking straight to God. He opens with “Hear my prayer, O LORD; let my cry for help come before You.”

cards.question: The worn-out man asks the LORD to take His time and answer him whenever He's ready.

cards.text: He begs God not to hide His face from him in his day of distress, and to “answer me quickly when I call.” Friend, this man isn't leaving a voicemail, he's ringing the doorbell AND knocking.

cards.question: Then the man tells God why he's in such a hurry. He says his days vanish like smoke. What's he saying about his life?

answers.text: Its troubles will blow over soon

cards.text: His bones burn like glowing embers. His heart is afflicted, and withered like grass.

cards.question: The man's heart is so worn down that he says he even forgets to ___ his bread.

cards.text: Through his loud groaning, his skin hangs on his bones. I live in a BAKERY with cookie dough on every spoon, so friend, I have NEVER forgotten to eat, not ONCE.

cards.question: The man calls himself a desert owl, an owl among the ruins, and a lone bird on a housetop. What do these pictures say about how he feels?

answers.text: He feels ready to fly home

cards.text: He says he lies awake, a lone bird up all night. Friend, I did years of that in the back of a junk drawer, and trust me, the view is MOSTLY dust.

cards.question: Besides feeling all alone, the man has enemies, but they only bother him once in a while.

cards.text: All day long they taunt him, ridicule him and curse him. He says he has eaten ashes like bread and mixed his drink with tears.

cards.question: The man has been eating ashes like bread and mixing his drink with tears. What does he say all this sorrow comes from?

answers.text: A long famine in the land

cards.question: The man says it was his enemies who picked him up and cast him aside.

cards.text: No, he tells the LORD, “You have picked me up and cast me aside.” Friend, as a stamper who got carried across a kitchen and tucked into a junk drawer, I FELT that one.

cards.question: The man says his days are like lengthening shadows. Then he goes back to the picture he used for his heart: “I wither away like ___.”

cards.text: Then the whole prayer turns on one little word: But. The man's days are like lengthening shadows, but the LORD is a whole different story.

cards.question: The man's own days are fading. What does he say about the LORD?

answers.text: He is far off and silent
He has grown tired of Zion

cards.text: His renown endures to all generations, too. Then the man turns to Zion, the city of Jerusalem, and tells the LORD He will rise up and have compassion on her.

cards.question: The man says Zion will have to wait a long time for the LORD's favor, because her appointed time hasn't come yet.

cards.text: Nope, “the appointed time has come.” God's servants delight in Zion's stones and take pity on her dust.

cards.question: When the LORD shows Zion favor, how will the nations and the kings of the earth respond?
God's servants take pity on Zion's dust. But the man says the LORD will ___ Zion.
Right after saying the LORD has appeared in His glory, the man says the LORD will despise the prayer of the destitute.

cards.text: No, He will turn toward their prayer, and “He will not despise their prayer.” Then the man wants all this written down for the generation to come.

cards.question: Why does the man want this written down for the generation to come?

answers.text: So people not yet created can praise the LORD
So everyone will remember his own name
So his enemies will finally go quiet

cards.text: I bet he never pictured a cookie stamper with a giant French mustache reading it, friend. Then he tells how the LORD looked down from the heights of His sanctuary, from heaven to earth.

cards.question: The LORD gazed out from heaven to earth. What did He look down to hear?
The LORD heard a prisoner's groaning. He also looked down to ___ those condemned to death.

cards.text: All so that they may proclaim the name of the LORD in Zion and praise Him in Jerusalem, when peoples and kingdoms assemble to serve the LORD. Friend, that's a LOT of people in one place, and not one of them is there for the cookies.
Then the man comes back to his own trouble: “He has broken my strength on the way; He has cut short my days.”

cards.question: His strength is broken and his days are cut short. What does the man ask God?

answers.text: Not to take him in the middle of his days
To take him home right away
To send his enemies far away

cards.text: Then he talks about God's years, which go on through all generations. In the beginning God laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of His hands.

cards.question: The earth and the heavens are the work of God's hands. What does the man say will happen to them?

answers.text: They will wear out like a garment
They will grow new every spring

cards.text: Then he tells God, “But You remain the same, and Your years will never end.” Friend, I wore out on a kitchen counter in a few years, and He outlasts the HEAVENS.

cards.question: The man ends his prayer by saying the children of God's servants will have to live in fear.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 15 quotes "I wither away like ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The joke uses two everyday images: leaving a voicemail is a phone, and ringing the doorbell and knocking is a door.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The card only restates verses 3 and 4 in plain words, with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: "Up all night" adds a time to the verse. Psalm 102:7 only says "I lie awake."

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The card only restates verses 8 and 9 in plain words, with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The right answer "God's indignation and wrath" uses the verse's own Bible wording. The wrong answers ("His own careless choices", "A long famine in the land") are plain modern phrasing, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card retells verse 11 ("The man's days are like lengthening shadows") but cites only Psalm 102:12.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The question links verse 16 to verse 14 with "But," which makes it a contrast with the servants' pity. The text links verse 16 with "For" ("For the LORD will rebuild Zion"). The card changes how the two lines connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card is only the verse 23 quote with a lead-in, with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card only restates verses 24 and 25 in plain words, with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: "I wore out on a kitchen counter in a few years" adds a timeframe to his backstory. The backstory says "Years of good baking" and "Over the years," with the cutters arriving one at a time and the daughter growing up, which points to many years.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 6 multiple choice, 3 true or false and 2 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: All six true or false cards in the walkthrough (stop 1 cards 2, 10 and 13; stop 2 cards 4, 8 and 20) have False as the right answer. A baker could learn to always pick False. The code shuffles answer position, but that doesn't help with true or false.
findings.question: Should there be a rule that true or false cards mix True and False right answers, so bakers can't learn a pattern?
